prompt: What does the browser do when it hydrates a page?
hint: The HTML is already there when it starts.

choices.text: Saves the page as a file for the next visit
choices.why: Writing a page to a file is prerendering, at build time.

choices.text: Asks the server to render the HTML a second time, and swaps it in once it arrives
choices.why: The server is not asked again; the browser does the work.

choices.text: Runs the same components over the HTML it received, and takes over
choices.why: Right: it attaches to the server's HTML rather than building it again.

choices.text: Downloads the page's data again and throws the HTML away
choices.why: It keeps the HTML; that is the point of rendering it on the server.

prompt: Match each page option with what it does.
hint: Two switch a half on and off; one moves the server's half in time.

pairs.right: The server sends an empty page
No JavaScript is sent to the browser
The page is rendered once, at build time

right_distractors: The page is rendered twice on the server

prompt: A page option is exported from a layout file. Which pages does it apply to?
hint: Think of how layouts nest.

choices.text: Every page under it, unless a page says otherwise
choices.why: Right: a page can override what its layout set.

choices.text: Every page of the application, whichever layout or group folder they happen to be in
choices.why: Only the root layout reaches every page.

choices.text: Only the pages that import the layout file in their own `<script>`
choices.why: Pages never import their layouts; the folders decide.

choices.text: Only the layout itself, never its pages
choices.why: A layout's value is inherited by what is under it.

prompt: Why does the lesson measure a build rather than the dev server?
hint: What does the dev server add to every page?

choices.text: A build is usually slower to answer, which makes the differences between the options easier to see
choices.why: Speed is not what is measured; what is sent is.

choices.text: The dev server cannot render pages on the server
choices.why: It renders on the server; lesson 13 watched it.

choices.text: Page options are ignored entirely in development
choices.why: They apply; the dev server only adds scripts of its own.

choices.text: The dev server adds its own scripts so it can update pages as you save
choices.why: Right: those would spoil a count of what a page really ships.

prompt: What does an adapter decide?
hint: It is the last step of the build.

choices.text: Which of the pages may be prerendered, and which must wait for a request
choices.why: Page options decide that, in the route files.

choices.text: The shape of what comes out, for a particular kind of host
choices.why: Right: a Node server, static files, or a platform's functions.

choices.text: Which components are compiled
choices.why: The compiling is the same for every host.

choices.text: Which version of Node the project needs to run on, and which packages it installs
choices.why: `engines` and the lockfile say that, not the adapter.

prompt: Why does the planner need `adapter-node` rather than one of the cloud adapters?
hint: Where are the sessions kept?

choices.text: Cloud adapters need TypeScript
choices.why: No adapter needs TypeScript.

choices.text: It reads and writes a file, so it needs one long-lived server with a disk
choices.why: Right: the data is a file beside the code.

choices.text: Cloud adapters cannot run form actions, so the forms of lesson 14 would stop working there
choices.why: They run actions; what they lack is a lasting disk.

choices.text: `adapter-node` is always the fastest choice
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given.

prompt: On which port does `node build` listen by default?
hint: Look at the line the server printed.

prompt: Why does `node build` belong in the project folder?
hint: The path in `planner.js` is relative.

choices.text: Port 3000 is only free there
choices.why: Ports have nothing to do with folders.

choices.text: Node refuses to run a file outside the folder it was started in
choices.why: Node runs it; the file it reads would be missing.

choices.text: The built server only works in the folder where the development `node_modules` was installed by npm
choices.why: The reason given is the data file.

choices.text: It reads `data/planner.json` relative to the folder it was started in
choices.why: Right: started elsewhere, it would look for the file elsewhere.

prompt: What is cross-site request forgery?
hint: Think of a page on another site, open in the same browser.

choices.text: Another site's page making your browser send a request to a site you use
choices.why: Right: the browser sends it, and the target cannot tell who meant it.

choices.text: Reading another site's cookies with a script
choices.why: A page cannot read another site's cookies; that is not this attack.

choices.text: Guessing a password by trying many in a row
choices.why: That is brute force.

choices.text: Copying a site's HTML and serving it at another address, so that visitors take it for the real one
choices.why: That is a copy, not a request sent in your name.

prompt: The header in which a browser says where the sending page came from is called ___.
hint: One word, capitalised in the request.

prompt: What status does a built SvelteKit server answer for a form posted from another origin?
hint: Forbidden.

prompt: The built server refused the planner's own form. Why?
hint: Compare the scheme it assumes with the one the browser sent.

choices.text: Port 3000 is not allowed to receive forms
choices.why: Ports are not checked on their own; the whole origin is.

choices.text: The action was missing from the built server
choices.why: It was there; the check ran before it.

choices.text: It assumed `https`, and the browser sent `http://localhost:3000`
choices.why: Right: with no proxy in front, the two origins did not match.

choices.text: The form had no `Origin` header at all, because it was sent by `look` rather than by a person
choices.why: `look` drives a real browser, which sends one.

prompt: What does the lesson advise about `csrf.trustedOrigins: ['*']` for a 403 like this one?
hint: What does `'*'` do to the check?

choices.text: To use it in development only, where it is harmless
choices.why: The dev server does not check at all, so it would change nothing there.

choices.text: To use it, since the planner has no login and no money, so there is nothing a forged form could harm
choices.why: A forged form would still save a session nobody asked for.

choices.text: To use it until the site has a certificate
choices.why: The lesson says never, with or without a certificate.

choices.text: Never to reach for it, and to give the server its own address instead
choices.why: Right: `'*'` turns the protection off; the cause was a server that did not know where it lives.

prompt: `paths: { origin: process.env.ORIGIN }` is in `vite.config.js`. When is `ORIGIN` read?
hint: When does `vite.config.js` itself run?

choices.text: When `node build` starts
choices.why: By then the value was built in long before.

choices.text: When the build starts, so the value is built in
choices.why: Right: that is why the lesson builds again with `ORIGIN=…`.

choices.text: Only when a form is posted
choices.why: Nothing in the config waits for a form.

choices.text: On every request, by the running server
choices.why: The config does not run in the built server.

prompt: With `ssr = false`, what was in the body the server sent for About?
hint: Read the `curl` output.

choices.text: The whole page, just as before
choices.why: That is what the default sends.

choices.text: The heading and the paragraph, but no header
choices.why: There was no heading either.

choices.text: One script, which renders the page in the browser
choices.why: Right: everything else was left to the browser.

choices.text: Nothing at all, an empty body
choices.why: There was a script in it.

prompt: Which of these does `ssr = false` cost a page? Choose all that apply.
hint: The lesson lists three.

choices.text: Nothing to see until the script has run
choices.why: Yes: the text is no longer in the first response.

choices.text: Nothing at all with JavaScript off
choices.why: Yes: `look --no-js` showed an empty body.

choices.text: Nothing for tools that read HTML and run no scripts
choices.why: Yes: some search engines and link previews.

choices.text: Its forms stop being able to post to actions
choices.why: Actions still run on the server; that is not one of the three.

prompt: When does `ssr = false` earn its place?
hint: Think of code that cannot run on a server.

choices.text: For a page that uses `window` or `document` while it renders
choices.why: Right: such a page cannot be rendered on the server at all.

choices.text: For any page that has a form
choices.why: Forms work best rendered on the server, as lesson 14 showed.

choices.text: For pages that must be found by search engines and shown in the previews of chat applications
choices.why: That is a reason against it.

choices.text: Whenever a page is small enough that rendering it in the browser costs little
choices.why: Size is not the question.

prompt: With `csr = false`, how many `<script>` tags did the server send for About?
hint: The first `grep -c` answered.

prompt: On About, with `csr = false`, what does "Back to the planner" do?
hint: Is there a router on the page?

choices.text: Loads the week as a new page, as an ordinary link does
choices.why: Right: no router is there to intercept the click.

choices.text: Nothing at all, since a link needs JavaScript to take the browser anywhere
choices.why: Links work without JavaScript; `look` followed it.

choices.text: A client-side navigation, the same as on every other page of the planner that has a router
choices.why: That needs the router, which About does not have.

choices.text: It asks before leaving the page
choices.why: Nothing asks; it is a plain link.

prompt: With `csr = false`, where does the `<script>` of each component on the page run?
hint: The HTML still has to be produced.

choices.text: In both places, as with the default
choices.why: That is the default, not this option.

choices.text: Nowhere: it is removed from the components
choices.why: It still runs, to produce the HTML.

choices.text: On the server only, the layout's included
choices.why: Right: the browser gets the result and nothing to run.

choices.text: In the browser only, after the HTML arrives
choices.why: No script is sent to the browser at all.

prompt: For which pages is `csr = false` safe, by the lesson's rule?
hint: Compare it with switching JavaScript off.

choices.text: Only pages that are prerendered
choices.why: It was safe on About before About was prerendered.

choices.text: Exactly where the page works with JavaScript off
choices.why: Right: for that page, JavaScript is off.

choices.text: Any page, as long as it has a stylesheet
choices.why: The stylesheet keeps the look, not the behaviour.

choices.text: Only pages with no links
choices.why: About has links, and they still work.

prompt: Which rule says whether a page may be prerendered?
hint: The documentation states it plainly.

choices.text: It must be smaller than a set size
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: It must have no load function, since nothing can be loaded while building
choices.why: Load functions can run at build time.

choices.text: It must ship no JavaScript at all, so that the file it becomes is only HTML and CSS
choices.why: A prerendered page can still hydrate, as `csr` says.

choices.text: Any two people asking for it must get the same content
choices.why: Right: one file has to be right for everybody.

prompt: The build wrote About to the file `build/prerendered/___`.
hint: Look at what `find` printed.

prompt: Why can the planner's own pages not be prerendered? Choose all that apply.
hint: The lesson gives three reasons.

choices.text: The week page reads `?week`, and at build time there is no address
choices.why: Yes: that is the error the build stopped on.

choices.text: Their content changes every time a session is added
choices.why: Yes: a file written at build would not see it.

choices.text: Their forms post to actions, which need a server listening
choices.why: Yes: nobody would answer the `POST`.

choices.text: They use components from `#lib`
choices.why: Where a component lives does not matter.

prompt: What is `prerender = 'auto'` for?
hint: Think of a blog with a thousand posts.

choices.text: Prerendering only in production builds
choices.why: That is not what it means.

choices.text: Rendering the page again every few minutes
choices.why: Nothing is rerendered on a timer.

choices.text: Prerendering the addresses the build finds, and rendering the rest on demand
choices.why: Right: the middle ground.

choices.text: Letting SvelteKit decide whether the page is safe to prerender
choices.why: It decides nothing; it allows both.

prompt: What did `adapter-static` report when the planner was built with it?
hint: Read the first line of its message.

choices.text: That `vite.config.js` was missing a `paths.origin`, so it could not tell where the site would live
choices.why: The origin was there; the routes were the problem.

choices.text: That About could not be prerendered, because it has `csr = false` set in its `+page.js`
choices.why: About was the one page that could.

choices.text: That Node 22 was too old for it
choices.why: The Node version was never mentioned.

choices.text: Two routes that are dynamic, the week and the course pages
choices.why: Right: they cannot be written to files.

prompt: Match each adapter with what it suits.
hint: Ask where the data lives.

pairs.right: An application with a server and a disk, like the planner
A site whose every page is the same for everybody
An application whose data is in a database

prompt: Why would the planner, as written, break quietly on a platform that runs functions per request?
hint: What happens to a file when the function stops?

choices.text: A file written there can vanish when the function stops, or go unseen by the next copy
choices.why: Right: and each copy would have its own queue too.

choices.text: Form actions are not allowed on functions
choices.why: Actions run; the data does not last.

choices.text: The CSRF check is usually switched off there
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: Those platforms refuse any code that imports `node:fs`
choices.why: Often they allow it; that is why the break is quiet.

prompt: About ends the lesson with `prerender = true` and `csr = false`. What does a visitor's browser get for `/about`?
hint: Combine the two options.

choices.text: HTML rendered on the server for this request, then hydrated by the router in the browser
choices.why: It was rendered at build, and nothing hydrates it.

choices.text: HTML written at build time, from a file, and no script
choices.why: Right: rendered once, and nothing to run.

choices.text: A redirect to the week page, since a prerendered page cannot be asked for directly
choices.why: Nothing redirects; the page is served.

choices.text: An empty page and a script that renders it
choices.why: That would be `ssr = false`.

prompt: Put the steps that got the planner's forms working on the built server in order.
hint: The origin is read when the build starts.
trap: Starting the server before the build would serve the old build, with the old origin.
